modules.summary: The rising curve with monospace callouts pinned to points on it.

usage.purpose: A narrative plotting frame: a Catmull-Rom spline drawn through hand-authored 0-100 percentage points, with HTML callout boxes pinned to the points that carry labels. The split is the whole design — the SVG is `aria-hidden` decoration and the callouts are an ordered list of real HTML, so the copy wraps, selects, finds, and is read in array order. It is for making an argument that has a *shape* (a rise, a dip, a recovery) where the copy is the payload and the curve is the frame the copy hangs on, not for showing measured values.
alsoFor: Falling, dipping, or S-shaped stories, not just the rising one. `y` runs from the top (0 = top), so any progression is just a different y sequence, and `stroke` picks from a 5-token union (`brand-peach`, `brand-peach-deep`, `accent-violet`, `accent-blue`, `semantic-matcha`) — a decline in `semantic-error-red` is the one thing NOT available, since red is not in `CurveStrokeToken`.

Denser callout layouts by alternating sides. `place` takes `above | below | left | right` and `align` takes `start | center | end`, so callouts can zig-zag above and below the sweep, and a node near the frame edge can anchor its box by its own left or right edge instead of hanging outside. `offset` (default 14px) tunes the gap for all of them at once.

Shaping the sweep without adding content: a point with `label` omitted is an anchor — no marker, no box, no entry in the `<ol>`. That is how you get a curve that runs edge to edge, or a deliberate valley between two labelled peaks, with only two or three actual callouts.

Reshaping the band via `aspect` (default 2), which sets both the wrapper's `aspectRatio` and the derived viewBox height. A wide hero strip (`aspect={4}`) or a squarer inline figure (`aspect={1.2}`) both scale uniformly because `preserveAspectRatio` is `xMidYMid meet`.

Rich callouts, not just strings. `label` is a `ReactNode`, so a box can hold a figure plus a caption, a `Chip`, or emphasis markup; per-point `className` merges into the callout `<li>`, which is the intended place to override the default `max-w-[62%]` width for one long box.
watchFor: No control-point API, and the spline is honest about it: the header states it can overshoot BETWEEN two points that are close in x and far apart in y. The documented fix is to spread the x values, not to fight it with anchors.

`aspect` is load-bearing, not layout sugar. The viewBox height is derived from it, and `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"` is chosen so node `<circle>`s stay circles — switching to `none` (the obvious way to fit an arbitrary box) scales x and y differently and renders every node as an ellipse. Setting a fixed height in `className` fights the inline `aspectRatio` style.

The callout boxes are deliberately opaque (`bg-surface-1`), because every box sits on a point that is ON the stroke by construction. Any translucency puts a peach line straight through the middle of a monospace label.

Reading order is array order, deliberately not sorted by x. The curve is `aria-hidden`, so the `<ol>` of callouts is the entire accessible content; reordering the `points` array for visual reasons silently reorders what a screen reader hears. Also note the boxes use mode-aware `surface.*` / `text.*`, so an always-dark instance inside a light page has to carry `dark` on its container.
notFor: Actual data visualisation. There is no scale, no axis, no data binding — every coordinate is a hand-placed percentage, and the path is generated from those percentages. If numbers drive the shape, this will drift from them silently; use a real chart.

A step sequence that happens to be labelled. If there is no curve carrying the argument, use `JourneyTrack` (state per step) or `PipelineStepper` (progress through a running job); for a plain numbered list on the dark page, the `NumberedStep` pattern.

modules.summary: The "ask us anything" prompt block — an attributed question, a box to answer

usage.purpose: The "ask us anything" prompt block: an attributed question rendered as the loud heading, a quiet borderless textarea that the heading labels via `aria-labelledby`, an AI-disclosure badge, and a small submit sized to its label in the bottom-right. It is the package's one genuinely interactive section — a controlled textarea plus a submit handler — and it lives in its own module specifically so `'use client'` does not spread to server-renderable siblings. The restraint is the design: it is a low-commitment probe, so a full-bleed primary button and a boxed input would make it read as a form rather than as a question.
alsoFor: Any single free-text capture on a dark page — a waitlist "what are you trying to fix?", a feedback prompt, a qualification question. `question`, `lede`, `placeholder` and `submitLabel` are all props and nothing in the file is Skene-specific.
Unattributed use: omit `avatar` and `name`. The header row keeps its `min-h-[32px]` so the block's rhythm holds and the badge stays put on the right.

Non-AI contexts: `showAiBadge={false}` when no model is involved or the surrounding section already discloses it. `aiBadgeLabel` is a node, so the chip can carry "BETA" or an icon instead — but note the default `true` is a disclosure decision, not a styling default.
Prefilled or externally driven text — it is fully controlled through `value` / `onValueChange`, so a parent can seed it with an example prompt, restore a draft, or clear it after submit.

Rendering with no handler at all: `onSubmit` is optional and the form always `preventDefault`s, so the block is safe in a gallery or preview with nowhere to submit (the gallery case does exactly this).
watchFor: `chrome.text.*` and `chrome.surface.*` throughout are correct ONLY because the panel paints its own invariant ground. Drop this inside a `light` surface (a `LightSectionCard`, a `Bridge` band) or swap the fill for a mode-aware one and every text class in here becomes cream on cream. The peach submit is the exception — `brand.peach` / `brand.peach-text` move together.

`'use client'` is on the module, so whoever owns `value` becomes a client component too. Keep the owner in an island file; the gallery has `islands.tsx` precisely so pulling this in does not move every server-rendered sibling off the server path.

There is no pending, disabled, or error state and no submit gating — the button fires `onSubmit('')` on an empty textarea as happily as on a filled one. Adding a `pending`/`disabled` prop is a small change, but it IS a change; do not assume it is there.

The question renders as a fixed `<h3>` whose `useId` id is the textarea's only accessible name. Fine mid-page, wrong if this block is a page's primary heading — there is no `as` or `headingLevel` prop, and adding one is the small addition you would need.
notFor: A real form — multiple fields, validation, or anything that posts to a route. The textarea has no `name`, the `<form>` has no `action`, and submit is always intercepted. Use the `ui/` primitives (`Textarea`, `Input`, `Button`) and own the form yourself.

A single-line capture like an email signup. The 104px `min-h`, `resize-none` textarea and clamp(1.6rem…2.35rem) heading are sized for a paragraph-length answer; for an email one-liner use an `Input` plus `Button` inside `FinalCta`'s `actions` slot.

Labels that carry a badge: since they are `ReactNode` and the row is `flex items-center gap-3`, `yearlyLabel={<>Billed yearly <Chip>-20%</Chip></>}` renders inline.

Driving more than one section from one switch. It holds no internal state, so a single `useState` in a page island can feed the `PlanGrid` prices and a comparison table from the same value — the demo (`docs-app/app/pricing-demo.tsx`) does exactly this pattern with one plan grid.

Labels use invariant `chrome.text.*` (`text-chrome-text-primary` when active). Correct only on an always-dark surface; on a cream panel the active label is cream on cream. It is not safe inside a featured `PlanCard` or a `LightSectionCard`.

The knob positions `left-1` and `left-[26px]` are hand-fitted to the track's `h-6 w-11` and the knob's `size-4`, and only `left` is transitioned. Resizing the track via `className` leaves the knob travelling to the wrong stop.
Controlled-only: there is no `defaultYearly` and no internal state. Omit `onChange` wiring and you ship a switch that visibly does nothing.
It is the client boundary. Deep-import `@skene/design-system/sections/billing-toggle` rather than pulling it from the root barrel next to server-rendered siblings.
notFor: A settings or form boolean — use `ui/switch` or `SettingsField`. This one has marketing-sized side labels, a pricing-specific hardcoded aria-label, and no form/name/id integration.
Three or more options (a third billing term, a segmented control). It is a two-state switch with `aria-checked`; use `ui/tabs` or the `PillNav` pattern instead.

modules.summary: The bridge: GTM ↔ Skene ↔ Engineering. A cream band carrying three cards in a

usage.purpose: A whole cream band (a `<section>`, not a card) that lays N `BridgeNode` cards in a row, interleaves arrows between them, and inverts one of them to dark and lifts it. It exists to argue POSITION — that the featured thing sits between the others — and the tone difference is the argument, not styling: three cards in one tone read as three peers and the band says nothing. Structurally it is also the package's one doubly-nested inversion (`light` band, `dark` card inside it), so it doubles as the worked example of how the two subtree switches nest.
alsoFor: Any node count, not just three. `Bridge` runs `Children.toArray` and emits N-1 arrows, and each node gets `flex-1 basis-0`, so a two-card before/after or a four-stage handoff works with no change.
A plain sequence band with no subject: omit `featured` on every `BridgeNode` and you get N peer cream cards joined by arrows — right for when the argument is order rather than position.
A cream heading block on a dark page. `eyebrow` + `title` + `lede` + `caption` render a centred, max-w-[880px] header independent of the cards; pass one child and no arrows are drawn at all.

`BridgeNode` is exported on its own and composes inside any other `light` surface (e.g. a `LightSectionCard` visual slot). Its non-featured styling — `bg-surface-0`, `border-chrome-line-on-light` — is written for a light ancestor.

Branding the subject card: `icon` takes any node (the live section uses a glyph, an inline SVG logo works), `items` takes three short fragments, and `title` composes with `<Accent>` because `brand.peach` is mode-aware and lands on its light value (#89684a) inside the band.
watchFor: The `light` class on the root is unconditional and written first, and the featured card's `dark` is the counterpart. `cn` is tailwind-merge, so a `className` background WILL win over `bg-brand-light` while leaving `light` in place — override the fill with anything dark and you get exactly the invisible-text failure (`text.primary` #faf1e9 on #faf1e9) the file header documents.

Arrows are unconditional between children — there is no prop to suppress them. Anything you pass as a child that is not part of a left-to-right sequence still gets an arrow after it unless it is last.

`featured` is a per-node boolean with nothing enforcing exactly one. Two featured cards render two dark lifted cards and the band loses its point. Also note the lift is `md:-translate-y-3`: below `md` the row stacks and the featured card is dark but not raised.

The kicker is a hand-rolled Eyebrow-SHAPED chip, deliberately not `<Eyebrow>` — `Eyebrow` is built from `chrome.surface.border` / `chrome.text.muted`, which are invariant and render near-invisible on cream. The same trap applies to anything you pass into any slot that uses `chrome.text.*`.

The outer cards' fill is `bg-surface-0` (mode-aware → #fafafa inside the band), deliberately a shade off the band's cream `brand.light`. Do not "fix" it to `bg-brand-light` — the cards then disappear into the band.
notFor: A generic 3-up feature or value grid. The arrows assert a relationship and the dark card asserts primacy; if you just want a row of peer cards use `ValueCards` (which argues by cost/gain contrast) or a plain grid of primitives.

Anything with state or progress. The arrows are static and `aria-hidden`, and there is no per-node status. For a job running now use `PipelineStepper` (done/active/pending); for funnel steps carrying health use `JourneyTrack`, whose connector is a gradient between the two states it joins.

modules.summary: The PR surface is a GitHub App that posts reviews; nothing ships as an Actions workflow.

usage.purpose: Four integration cards on a textured field, cycling detail copy with GSAP: MCP server, GitHub App, Cloud API, and repo audit. Ported from skene-marketing-website's CardAnimationIntegrations.
alsoFor: The visual slot of a cream band — drop it in `LightSectionCard.visual` or `IntegrationsHighlight`, which is the pre-composed homepage band.
Custom card or detail sets by passing `cards` and `details`; defaults match the live marketing animation.
A different halftone field via `backgroundImage`; defaults to `assetUrls.integrationsField`.
watchFor: Client-only: uses GSAP and ScrollTrigger. Importing it pulls a client boundary at this file.
Cards and detail panel start at `visibility: hidden`; GSAP drives `autoAlpha`. Do not remove that or the first paint flashes every card.
notFor: A static 2x2 grid where every detail is visible at once. Use this when you need motion and one active card at a time.
A row of tiles with a single detail panel under the chosen one.

modules.summary: The rule-separated feature list with a peach check.

usage.purpose: The rule-separated feature list with a peach check — the single highest-frequency element on a Skene marketing page, previously hand-written at every call site. `CheckList` is a bare `<ul>` that sets one CSS variable (`--check-rule`); `CheckItem` is an `<li>` whose separator is a *top border on each row* rather than a divider element, so a list of one still reads as part of its card instead of floating. The check is a real `aria-hidden` `<span>`, not a `::before`, precisely so a screen reader does not announce "tick" before every line.
alsoFor: Any proof list in a section body, not just plan cards — the gallery uses it directly inside `FeatureRow` (dark, no flags) and inside `LightSectionCard` (`onLight`).
Requirement / "what you get" lists on light product chrome: nest it in a `ProductWindow` (whose `tone="light"` default carries the `light` class) and pass `onLight`.
Rows with structure, not just strings. `CheckItem` children are `ReactNode`, so links, `<strong>`, or a trailing `<Chip>` all render, and the aria-hidden glyph keeps the announcement clean.
Two densities on the same page: `dense` (13px, `py-[11px]`) for card interiors, the default (14px, `py-3`) for section copy.
Per-row tweaks via `className` on `CheckItem` — `cn` is tailwind-merge, so `border-t-0` on the first row or a different `py-*` actually replaces the base utility.
watchFor: `dense` does not propagate. It is a separate prop on `CheckList` (margin) and on `CheckItem` (padding + type size); set it on both or you get tight spacing with 14px text.

`onLight` does NOT create the light context — it only chooses between `--color-chrome-line-on-light` and `--color-chrome-line-subtle` for the rule. The peach check and the `text.*` type invert only if a `light` ancestor exists (featured `PlanCard`, `LightSectionCard`, light `ProductWindow`). On a bare cream `<div>` you must add `light` yourself, as the gallery case does.
The rule colour is an inline `style={{ borderTopColor: 'var(--check-rule)' }}` on every item, so a `border-*` colour utility in `className` will not override it — re-set `--check-rule` instead.

Every item carries `border-t`, including the first, so the list always opens with a hairline. That is intentional inside a card; strip it with `className="border-t-0"` on the first `CheckItem` if the list stands alone.
Type is `text-text-muted-strong` (theme-aware) by design — swapping in a `chrome.text.*` class reintroduces the exact bug the header warns about.
notFor: An interactive checklist or to-do list. There is no checked state, no input, and the glyph is `aria-hidden` — use `ui/checkbox` (or `SettingsField`) for anything the user toggles.

An included/not-included comparison. The ✓ glyph and its `text-brand-peach` colour are hardcoded with no icon or tone prop; a cross/dash row would need a code change (e.g. a `tone`/`icon` prop on `CheckItem`). `ComparisonTable`'s `TableCheck` / `TableDash` already do this.

modules.summary: The 10px monospace chip.

usage.purpose: The 10px monospace uppercase rectangle, extracted from two copies that were written independently — `PlanCard`'s inline tier span and `ProductWindow`'s `WindowStatus` — which had already drifted apart on tracking before anyone noticed. Its job is to hold the geometry still: `tone` carries colour and nothing else, with tracking as the single declared exception. It exists as much to stop a third inline copy being written as to render the two that exist.
alsoFor: An identity marker on either ground with `tone="neutral"`. This is the one tone allowed to use invariant `chrome.surface-darker` / `brand.light`, because its fill is near-black on both the dark page AND the featured cream `PlanCard` — there is no inversion for an invariant token to get wrong.

A state marker inside a light surface with `tone="healthy"` (matcha) or `tone="live"` (violet). Both derive their fill through `color-mix` from mode-aware tokens, so they follow a `light` ancestor down to the light value rather than laying a dark-mode tint on cream — safe inside a light `ProductWindow` body or a cream card.

Wrapping in a narrower-vocabulary named component. `WindowStatus` (product-window.tsx:97) is the sanctioned template: it restricts `tone` to `'healthy' | 'live'`, pins its tracking override, and keeps the name callers actually look for. Do that again rather than adding an inline chip.
Matching an already-shipped rendering. `className` merges last via `cn`, so a `tracking-*` utility beats the base 0.08em — the documented, and only documented, override.
Non-string content: `children` is a `ReactNode`, so a glyph plus a word, or a count, works. `shrink-0` is in the base, so the chip is safe as the fixed item in a flex row opposite a title that wraps.

A breakage or defect marker with `tone="danger"`. Its recipe deviates from `healthy`/`live` on purpose: the ink is the on-tint token (`--color-semantic-error-red-on-tint`), the split `StatPill` and `Finding` both shipped without and measured below the floor for, and the tint is 12% — inside the band those tokens were measured for. Both halves are mode-aware, so it holds inside a light `ProductWindow` as well as on the page.

A caution marker with `tone="warn"` (amber): present but degraded, deprecated, or waiting on a decision. Same corrected recipe as `danger` — amber on-tint ink over a 12% tint — added because two marketing pages were retinting `tone="neutral"` through a shared amber `className`, base ink on a 15% fill, which is the inline fork plus the measured-band miss in one constant.
watchFor: `className` merges last and therefore beats the base for *any* utility, but `tracking-*` is the only override this package sanctions. Changing `px-[7px]`, `py-1`, `rounded-[5px]` or `text-[10px]` at a call site re-forks the component the extraction exists to prevent.

Tracking is unreconciled on purpose: `Chip` holds the tier chip's 0.08em and `WindowStatus` overrides back to 0.05em, because both values shipped and were signed off in the browser. "Fixing" either one silently restyles a verified surface — about 5px across "DASHBOARD: HEALTHY", per the note at the override.
`healthy` and `live` set their colour in an inline `style` from the `TONES` table, so a `text-*` utility in `className` will not override them. Only `neutral` colours via classes.

Adding a tone is a row in `TONES`, never a branch at the call site — and the file's stated rule is to add one only the day something actually renders it. If you add a light-filled tone, do not copy `neutral`'s invariant `chrome.*` licence; that exemption depends on the fill being near-black on both grounds.
notFor: General status on a product surface. `Badge` (ui) is the shadcn primitive for that; `Chip` is section furniture locked at 10px mono, and stretching it to product use will produce pressure to make the geometry variable — the one thing it is here to prevent.
A pill beside a heading. `StatChip` (a fact) or `MetaChip` (a promise) own that slot at `rounded-full` 12px; `WindowStatus` owns the window title bar's right-hand slot.

modules.summary: The inline identifier chip: an event name, a column, a flag, a path.

usage.purpose: The inline identifier chip inside a sentence: an event name, a column, a flag, a path. Extracted from SEVEN copies — six byte-identical component declarations across skene-site route files, verified by comparing the emitted class string, plus a seventh spelling as `PROSE_CODE`, the same recipe as a descendant selector for prose the author cannot reach element by element. The oldest open entry on that repository's gap list, on a site where an event name appears in nearly every paragraph of body copy.
alsoFor: Prose the caller does not author element by element — MDX, a table cell, a body rendered from a string. Applied to the CONTAINING block rather than each mark, because there is no `<code>` to wrap. Kept as a second mechanism deliberately: merging it into the component would leave that case with no answer.
notFor: Anything block-level. `TerminalBlock` renders a command as its own surface; this mark sits INSIDE running text at body size, and takes the body contrast floor rather than the large-text one because of it.

A status or identity marker beside text. `Chip` is padded and sized to sit NEXT TO a sentence at 10px mono; this sits in one at body size. Reaching for `Chip` here produces pressure to make its geometry variable, which is the one thing it exists to prevent.
A theme-neutral status marker. `Badge` is shadcn's and neutral by construction; this carries brand ink on a brand surface, which is why it is a section rather than a primitive.

modules.summary: The capability comparison: one row per claim, one column per approach, with

usage.purpose: A real semantic `<table>` for capability comparison — one row per claim, one column per approach, with your column picked out. The featured column is washed in the head *and* every body cell so it reads as one continuous object top to bottom, and the header additionally turns peach so its identity is stated once in words rather than only in colour. The whole component is really the pairing of `min-width: 820px` on the table with `overflow-x: auto` + `tabIndex={0}` on the wrapper: a comparison that reflows into stacked cards stops being a comparison, so on narrow screens it keeps its shape and scrolls sideways instead.
alsoFor: A plan or pricing feature matrix. `columns` and each row's `cells` are `React.ReactNode[]`, so prices, phrases and glyphs all drop in; `featuredIndex` marks the recommended plan.
A plain spec sheet with nothing highlighted — omit `featuredIndex` and no wash renders anywhere, head or body.

The same table on a cream band, via `onLight` — the only polarity prop, and it switches exactly one thing: `--table-rule` from `chrome.line.subtle` to `chrome.line.onLight`. Everything else is mode-aware already.

Highlighting a different column on one row: `ComparisonRow` accepts its own `featuredIndex`, and the table's injection uses `child.props.featuredIndex ?? featuredIndex`, so an explicit per-row value wins.

`ComparisonRow` rendered outside a `ComparisonTable` (its `featuredIndex` prop is documented for exactly this), and `TableCheck`/`TableDash` reused anywhere as accessible yes/no glyphs — both take a `label` prop precisely so a translated page can replace the English default.
A footnote or source line under the table via `caption` — it is a real `<caption>` with `[caption-side:bottom]`, so it names the table for assistive tech and reads as a note visually.
watchFor: Never put `min-w-*` on the wrapper or `overflow` on the table. The source calls this out: swap them and the page body scrolls horizontally instead of the panel. `className` lands on the wrapper, so a stray `min-w` there is the easy mistake.

`featuredIndex` indexes `columns` *including* the leading row-header column, while body cells compute `featuredIndex === i + 1`. That is intentional (one index space for both) but it means `featuredIndex={0}` washes the header cell and nothing in the body — a half-marked column. Valid values start at 1.

Column widths are `w-[40%]` for the row header and `w-[20%]` for every other column regardless of how many there are. It is tuned for three answer columns; five answer columns declares 140% and the browser renegotiates it.

`featuredIndex` reaches rows by `cloneElement` over `Children.toArray`, not by context (deliberately — `createContext` would drag this static table across the client boundary to pass one number). Rows must be direct, valid element children: wrap them in a Fragment or a wrapper component and the injection silently stops. Similarly, the last-row rule removal is `[&>tr:last-child>*]:border-b-0` on the `<tbody>`, so a `<tfoot>` or an extra element in there breaks it.

The accessibility contract is load-bearing and easy to erode: `<th scope="col">` in the head, `<th scope="row">` per row, and glyph cells carrying an `sr-only` word — a cell whose entire content is `aria-hidden` reads as "no data", not "no". Keep `label` populated when you pass custom markers.
notFor: An interactive or long data table — sorting, pagination, selection, hundreds of rows. This is static markup with no `use client`; use the `ui/table` primitive on a product surface.
A pricing layout where each column needs its own frame, tier chip and CTA button. That is `PlanCard`; a table column cannot hold an action.

modules.summary: The discovery artifact: Skene Cloud's Events table, drawn rather than

usage.purpose: The discovery artifact: the events Skene found, where it found them, and whether each one verified.
alsoFor: Any found-things table with a per-row state — files scanned, endpoints discovered, records matched. Every column header is a prop and every cell is a node.
A table with no header bar at all: title, source, summary and actions are all optional and the window drops the bar when they are absent.
watchFor: `foundAt` is the column allowed to be empty, and an empty cell is what breaks a table's alignment. The gallery case carries a row without one for that reason.
notFor: A list of evaluations rather than of found events. That is EvaluatorList, which is the same window with a different column contract.

A settings or reference table, or any table of three columns or fewer. That is KeyValueTable's job — it owns per-column formatting at two densities and a headerless `<dl>` rendering — while this module is the fixed four-column discovery artifact: event, type, where it was found, whether it verified. Narrowing it re-derives KeyValueTable with the discovery chrome attached.

modules.summary: The evaluator's Check tab: a metric, the formula under it, one row per

usage.purpose: The evaluator's Check tab: a metric, the formula under it, one row per operand, and the results it produced.
alsoFor: Any computed-value explanation — a score, a rate, a derived KPI. The formula is a slot, so the operands can be anything.
A metric with no formula at all: pass `metric` and `results` and leave the middle out.
watchFor: CheckChip and TagChip are the same 11px mono tag under two names — recorded as a known duplicate in the source rather than laundered.
notFor: The requirements a signal must meet, rather than the arithmetic. That is EvaluatorVerify.
A single score with no working shown. That is ScoreRing.

modules.summary: The Evaluator index: every evaluation in a workspace, and whether the signals

usage.purpose: The evaluator index: every evaluation in a workspace, and whether the signals it depends on were found.
alsoFor: Any status list with a per-row check — jobs, monitors, integrations tests. Four columns, all named by prop.
Unframed, by passing `frame={false}` — the textured field is a placement decision, not a property of the artifact.
watchFor: EvaluatorNote is exported from here and re-typed in three other files. Import it rather than adding a fourth copy.
notFor: The two-pane version, list beside detail. That is EvaluatorPanel.
Found events rather than evaluations. That is DiscoveryTable.

modules.summary: The whole Evaluator surface in one window: the index of evaluations, and one

usage.purpose: The two-pane evaluator: the index on one side, one evaluation's requirements on the other.
alsoFor: Any master-detail artifact where the detail is a checklist — a rule and its conditions, a policy and its clauses.
The same list as EvaluatorList with a different detail pane, since `list` and `detail` are independent props.

The marketing wireframes' side-by-side cut with `split`: the index in a dark left pane (the package's own `dark` subtree switch, nested inside the window's forced `light` the way the product nests its sidebar) with `activeIndex` picking out the open row, the requirements in the cream right pane. Stacks back below `md`.
watchFor: Its VerifyRow and MetaPill are copied line-for-line from evaluator-verify. The source says so and defers the merge; do not add a third copy.

In `split` mode the index renders at lower resolution — name and confirmed count per row; the check pill and metric belong to the stacked table. A caller needing all four columns beside the detail has outgrown the split and wants two windows.
notFor: Only the requirements, with no index beside them. That is EvaluatorVerify.

modules.summary: The Evaluator's Verify tab: a list of the signals an evaluation needs, each

usage.purpose: The requirements an evaluation depends on: one row per event, its verdict, and the fields it must carry.
alsoFor: Any requirements checklist with nested sub-requirements — a schema contract, a compliance list, a validation report.
A flat list, by omitting `fields` on every requirement: the indent is what says which row to read, so uniform rows are a deliberate choice.
watchFor: `tags` is free-form because the package does not know the product's vocabulary. That is also why nothing validates them.
notFor: The same rows with the index beside them. That is EvaluatorPanel.

modules.summary: The FAQ band: a heading column that stays put, and the questions beside it.

usage.purpose: The FAQ band: a heading column that stays put, and the questions beside it on a cream ground with a hairline per row and a round toggle.
alsoFor: Any disclosure band on a marketing page — objections, a glossary, what's included.
Many rows open at once, via `multiple`, when the answers are short enough to scan together.

A heading column that closes with a CTA: `actions` renders under the note (or under the title when there is no note), so the wireframes' head button beside the questions no longer needs a hand-built column. Pass the variant that survives the cream ground — the same inversion caveat as the answers' links.
watchFor: `light` on the root is unconditional and there is no dark variant. The band ships in one tone because every FAQ on both surfaces is the cream one.
It composes Radix directly rather than ui/accordion, whose trigger bakes in a chevron where this band's mark is a round plus.
notFor: A disclosure list on a product surface. That is ui/accordion, the primitive underneath.
A static teaser grid of questions with no disclosure. That is QuestionGrid.

modules.summary: The alternating feature row: copy on one side, a visual on the other, flipping

usage.purpose: A whole dark band of a page: a copy column (corner marker, ringed icon, title, italic lede, proof list, pinned actions) beside a visual panel, mirrored per row by `reverse`. The shape is an argument, not a layout — `title` + `lede` are the promise and `children` (usually a `CheckList`) is the proof, which is why the lede is its own slot rather than the first paragraph of the body. Ships with `FeatureStack` (the `grid gap-6` rhythm wrapper) and `FeatureIcon` (a ringed accent glyph in peach/violet/blue) so a three-row feature section is three prop sets rather than a re-derived grid.
alsoFor: A one-off split band anywhere on the page — used without `FeatureStack`, with `n` and `icon` omitted, it is just copy-beside-visual; nothing couples it to a numbered list.

A copy-only band with no product surface at all. Omit `visual`, `texture` and `textureSrc` and the row drops its second cell, its 600px floor and its split grid class, so it is one column sized to its copy rather than a half-filled card. This is what lets a page of mixed bands read as one object: skene-site has 21 copy-only bands against 29 with visuals, and until 0.9.18 the copy-only ones sat bare on the page ground beside bordered cards. `splitAt` and `reverse` go inert rather than erroring, so a consumer can pass them uniformly across a mixed set.

A grid cell's own type scale: `titleScale="cell"` renders the title at `--font-size-card-title` (20px), the token skene-site's cards already carried. Added in 0.9.20 with the grid-cell role, because `row` is a 28-40.8px clamp and `/resources/glossary`'s eighteen terms would each have had a heading larger than the section heading above them.

A cell in a 2-up or 3-up grid of small cards, which `ui/card` used to own on marketing pages. Since 0.9.19 `render_marketing_cards_as_feature_row` makes this the only marketing card, and the copy-only path is what makes it affordable: a cell with no visual has no 600px floor, so skene-site's 18 glossary terms stay near their 159px each instead of becoming 11,232px of stacked bands. One component, and deliberately not one picture - a copy-only cell and a row with a visual are the same card at two densities.

The band that used to be cream. `LightSectionCard` keeps its export and its `light` mechanism for product and gallery use, but a marketing page that alternates one repeating object cannot also alternate polarity without the cream band reading as a second system. Removing `light` from such a call site is not cosmetic: every mode-aware token in the subtree keeps its dark value against a cream fill, and `text.primary` lands at #faf1e9 on #faf1e9, which is absent rather than dim.

Framing something other than a ProductWindow: `visual` is an unconstrained ReactNode, so an ``, a `Terminal`, an `AnnotatedCurve` or a chart all drop in, and omitting `texture`/`textureSrc` gives a plain `p-[34px]` panel instead of a halftone field.

Non-Skene artwork behind the visual: `textureSrc` takes any URL and overrides `texture`, so a consumer with its own texture gets the same inset behaviour without touching the three bundled site fields.

Body content that is not a checklist — `children` gets a full-width wrapper (deliberately `w-full`, not the prose measure) so a small table, a rule-separated spec list, or paragraphs reach the column edge.
Reusing `FeatureIcon` on its own: it is a separate export taking `accent`, `className` and any `children` glyph or SVG, so the same three-way colour coding works in cards or lists elsewhere.
Any marker in the corner slot: `n` is a ReactNode, so "01", "Step 3", a date, or a small `Eyebrow` all render in the mono top-right position.
watchFor: Dark-surface only. The root is `bg-chrome-surface-1` and the title uses `text-chrome-text-primary` — invariant `chrome.*` tokens that by definition cannot follow a `light` ancestor (docs/sections.md rule 1). Adding `light` to `className` will not invert it.

`min-h-[600px]` applies at every breakpoint, and `actions` is pinned with `mt-auto` against that height. A short row will be mostly whitespace; `cn` is twMerge so `className="min-h-0"` wins, but then the actions pinning stops meaning anything.

`reverse` only takes effect at `md:` (it sets `md:col-start-*`) — below md the copy column is always first. And it must be set explicitly per row: deriving it from an index breaks the moment a row is inserted or reordered, and these rows are content.

There is an always-on sheen over the visual cell — an `aria-hidden pointer-events-none` span with a hardcoded white 135° gradient. It is not a prop and cannot be switched off; harmless over a mock, visible over a photograph.
notFor: A container on a PRODUCT surface — a workspace panel, a settings block, anything inside Skene Cloud. `render_marketing_cards_as_feature_row` in machine/rules.yaml scopes this component to marketing pages and nothing else; `ui/card` remains the generic product container it has always been.

A panel INSIDE a drawn artifact. An artifact's own chrome is `AppPanel` within `ArtifactShell`; this component is what the artifact sits in, not what it is made of. Nesting one in the other puts a 600px marketing band inside a depiction.

modules.summary: The closing band: full-bleed, centred, one heading and the actions.

usage.purpose: The closing band: full-bleed, centred, one large heading, an optional lede and an actions row, over a textured dark backdrop. It appears twice on the live homepage and once per subpage, and every instance had previously been rebuilt by hand. The default backdrop (`pixel-bg.webp`, 143 KB) ships with the package and is resolved from the module itself, on the principle that the default should produce the section the site actually has rather than a stripped-down gradient the caller has to re-dress.
alsoFor: Any full-bleed closing band, not just signup — `children` is the heading node and `actions` is a free slot, so waitlist, newsletter, "book a demo", or an end-of-doc band all fit without changes.
Per-page texture: `backdrop` takes any URL string (including a `data:` URI); `backdrop={false}` renders the gradient alone for a quieter band on a page that already has texture.

Non-button actions. The wrapper is `flex flex-col … sm:flex-row gap-3`, so an email input plus a submit button, or a client `<form>` island, drops in as `actions` while the band itself stays a server component.
Height and rhythm tuning via `className` — `min-h-*` and padding merge through tailwind-merge, so `min-h-[380px]` makes a mid-page band out of the same component.
watchFor: Every colour is an inline `style`: the section background (`--color-chrome-surface-deep`) and the `linear-gradient(...) , url(...)` scrim with `saturate(70%)`. Utility classes in `className` lose to inline styles, so you cannot recolour or re-scrim it from the call site.
All type uses invariant `chrome.text.*`. This band is dark by construction — adding `light` will not invert it and will break any mode-aware node you pass into `actions`.

The heading is a hardcoded `<h2>` at `clamp(2.75rem, 5vw, 5rem)`. A page that needs this to be its `<h1>`, or a visibly smaller heading, needs a prop addition (`as`/`headingLevel`) rather than a class.

The default backdrop resolves via `new URL('../../assets/pixel-bg.webp', import.meta.url)`. Bundlers that understand that pattern (Next included) emit a real asset URL; one that does not will emit a broken path — pass an explicit URL or `false` as the escape hatch.
`min-h-[560px]` / `md:min-h-[610px]` plus `py-[90px]`: it is a whole band and will dominate a short page.
notFor: A cream or inverted CTA panel, or an inline mid-page CTA card — use `LightSectionCard`, which is the documented choice for "a cream panel with copy and buttons" and carries the `light` class properly.
A hero. The fixed dark scrim, `<h2>`, and centred single-column layout are closing-band shape; use `DitheredMedia` for a full hero composition or `HeroBackdrop` for a hero strip.

modules.summary: The audit primitives: a headline metric, its trend, and the per-step findings

usage.purpose: Three small pieces that together fill a product window with Skene's actual argument: `Finding` (a status-tagged row — tag, title, consequence), `MetricCard` (the headline number with a coloured delta), and `Sparkline` (an authored bar shape). The point of the set is the contradiction — a metric that looks fine above a list of steps that are unmeasured or renamed — so the status vocabulary is fixed at `good | warn | danger` bound to `semantic.matcha / warningAmber / errorRed`, the same three the dashboard uses. All content is props; nothing here knows what a Skene finding says.
alsoFor: Any KPI tile: `MetricCard` takes `label`, `value`, `delta` and `trend` as ReactNodes and has no light/dark flag at all — it inherits colour from its parent — and `children` is an open slot under the number for whatever the caller wants there.

Status rows on the dark page: `Finding onLight={false}` switches the card to `chrome.line.subtle` / `chrome.surface.2` / `chrome.text.primary`, which is what you want directly on the page ground or inside a `tone="dark"` ProductWindow.
Labelled list rows generally — `tag` is a ReactNode, not a number, so "GAP", "01", "P2" or "PII" all work; the same row shape serves audit results, a check-run summary, or a release-note list.
A compact one-line variant: `note` is optional, and with it omitted the grid collapses to tag plus title with no second row.

`Sparkline` on its own: it is a pure `bars: number[]` (clamped 0–100) plus a `highlight` index with no dependency on `MetricCard`, and `className` merges last (twMerge) so its `h-[74px]` and `mt-6` defaults are adjustable in a table cell or a card footer.
watchFor: `Finding`'s tag column is a hard `grid-cols-[68px_1fr]`. The tag does not widen the column — a longer string wraps or overflows inside 68px, and the type is 9px mono uppercase sized for roughly "STEP 3".

`onLight` defaults to **true**, the opposite of most flags in this package, because the default frame is a light `ProductWindow`. Put a `Finding` on the dark page without `onLight={false}` and you get a white card. Note also that the light case is `bg-white`, not the cream `brand.light` of its parent — deliberate, so the card floats on the window's fill.

`Sparkline` is `aria-hidden` and is explicitly not a chart: no axes, no scale, and `highlight` is an index because the copy decides which bar matters, not the data. Anything a reader must actually read has to live in `MetricCard`'s `value` or `delta`.

`MetricCard`'s `trend` defaults to `'danger'`, so an unspecified delta renders red; and its numeral is intentionally `font-normal` at 2.6rem with tight tracking, because bolding it makes the page read like a dashboard instead of an argument about one.
notFor: Real data visualization. `Sparkline` has no scale, axes, tooltips or empty state, and its values are authored — reach for an actual charting component when the numbers are measured.

Product-surface status inside the app. These are marketing components with hardcoded typographic scale and no loading/empty states; `ui/badge` is the shadcn status primitive for product surfaces (and `Eyebrow` is the section kicker — the three are not interchangeable).

modules.summary: The flows path: the dominant route through a product, drawn as a line of

usage.purpose: Nodes in a row joined by arrows, with a value and a note on each edge.
alsoFor: Any pipeline or path with a measurable step-to-step drop — a funnel, a queue, a state machine.
A plain sequence with unlabelled edges: `value` and `meta` are both optional.
watchFor: It scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping, so a long chain stays a chain. That is deliberate and a wrap would read as two flows.
notFor: Progress through named stages, with done/active/pending states. That is PipelineStepper.
Proportional bars rather than nodes. That is Funnel.

modules.summary: Site footer: a brand column, link columns, a bottom bar, and the oversized

usage.purpose: The site footer as a set of composable parts — `SiteFooter` (brand column, link columns, bottom bar), `FooterColumn`, `FooterLink`, `SocialLinks`, `SocialLink`. The part actually worth reusing is the oversized wordmark: 29vw at 1.7% opacity, clipped by the footer's own `overflow-hidden`, so it reads as texture at a glance and only resolves into a word if you look. Rendering it at a "sensible" size or opacity is the obvious change and it is wrong every time.
alsoFor: The sub-components stand alone. `FooterColumn` is a self-contained `<nav>` with its own heading and grid, so a link cluster works in a mega-menu, a sitemap block, or a docs index without `SiteFooter` around it.

Router-aware links: `FooterColumn` children are `ReactNode`, so `next/link` (or any framework Link) can be used directly where client-side navigation matters — `FooterLink` is a plain `<a href>` with no `asChild`.
A bar-only footer. `brand`, `wordmark`, `copyright` and `legal` are all optional and the bottom bar only renders when `copyright || legal` is present, so a minimal legal strip is reachable.
`wordmark` takes any `ReactNode` — a product name, a single tagline word, an inline SVG — and it is `aria-hidden`, so it never enters the accessibility tree whatever you put there.
`brand` is a free slot: logo plus copy plus `SocialLinks` in the demo, but a newsletter form or a status badge fits the same column (`col-span-full lg:col-span-1`).
watchFor: `FooterColumn` does `aria-label={String(title)}`. Pass a string. Pass JSX and every column's landmark is labelled "[object Object]" — the gallery case casts `title as string` for this reason.

The link grid template is `lg:grid-cols-[1.7fr_repeat(3,1fr)]` — sized for brand plus exactly three columns — and it sits on an inner `<div>` that has no `className` hook. `className` lands on the `<footer>` root, so you cannot retemplate the columns from the call site; a fourth column wraps to a second row.
The wordmark's `color: rgba(255,255,255,0.017)` is an inline style, so `text-*` utilities cannot touch it, and the value is deliberate — see the file header before "fixing" it.
`overflow-hidden` on the root is what clips the wordmark, and it will equally clip anything absolutely positioned that you put in `brand` (a popover, a tooltip, a dropdown).
Everything is invariant `chrome.*` (`bg-chrome-surface-deep-2`, `chrome-text-muted-warm`), so the whole component assumes an always-dark page.
`SocialLink` requires `label` — the child is an icon, so without it the link has no accessible name. That requirement is in the type; do not work around it.
notFor: An in-app or workspace footer, or any footer on a light page. The invariant `chrome.*` tokens cannot invert; build product-surface footers from `ui/card` / plain nav markup.
Primary site navigation. `FooterColumn` is a column of quiet 14px links with a label-sized `<h2>`; use the `PillNav` pattern from `patterns/marketing` for the top bar.

modules.summary: The activation funnel: a chart that reports healthy while the collection layer

usage.purpose: The activation funnel as the reader's own dashboard would draw it: one bar per step, and three states because a broken number is not a low number.
alsoFor: Any staged conversion chart where some steps are untrustworthy — onboarding, checkout, a signup path.
A plain proportional bar chart, by leaving every row `ok` and passing `fill`.
watchFor: `broken` renders a hatch, not a short solid bar, and `unknown` renders an empty dashed track with no fill element at all. A zero bar would be a lie, which is why the value cell says not measured instead of 0.
It is built on the light app window on purpose: this chart is the reader's own tool, not a Skene screen. Giving it a Skene crumb breaks the argument.
notFor: A small label/value/bar readout beside a journey track. That is MiniFunnel.
A determinate control-surface bar. That is ui/progress.

modules.summary: The round disc a glyph sits in at the head of a row: a circle, a hairline, a

usage.purpose: The round disc a glyph sits in at the head of a row: a circle, a hairline, a peach mark centred in it, `aria-hidden` always. It is the disc `TrustFact` draws, lifted out so it is reachable without the `<li>`, the separating rule and the qualifier slot that come with a fact row. `tone` picks the ground — `tint` is the cream-panel pair (`chrome.line.onLight` over a 12% peach wash), `muted` is the themed pair that follows the page — and `size` is one number, written to `style` so the glyph inside keeps whatever type size it inherits.
alsoFor: Any icon-led row, on cream or on the page ground: a status glyph, a numbered marker, a two- or three-letter code. Nothing here knows what the mark means, and the disc still renders when `children` is empty — which is what keeps a stack of rows aligned on their titles when only some of them carry one.
The 32px events-row badge skene-site keeps a local file for: `size={32}` with `tone="muted"` and `font-mono` through `className` is that component, exactly.
A quiet initials or code disc — two or three characters, `tone="muted"`. At that point it is a circle with the themed border over `bg-muted` and carries no state at all.
watchFor: `size` is written to `style`, following `ScoreRing`, so a `size-*` / `h-*` / `w-*` utility passed through `className` cannot beat it: inline styles win and `cn` does not merge across the two. Pass the number.

`tint` is cream-only. Its hairline is `chrome.line.onLight` — the invariant dark rule made for a cream fill — and its wash is a 12% peach mix written inline. On the dark page that border is all but gone; `muted` is the tone for a themed ground.

`aria-hidden` is unconditional and there is no prop to lift it. Every glyph this has held is decoration beside a real title, and announcing "check mark" before the sentence only delays it. If your mark IS the content — an avatar identifying a person — it needs an element that will be read out.

Nothing scales with `size`. The glyph takes the ambient type size, because a tick and a three-letter city code do not want the same one — which is also why `TrustFact`'s 38px rendering did not move when the disc was extracted.
notFor: The mark that carries a feature row's identity. `FeatureIcon` is 44px with an accent-tinted border at 47%, a 7px inset ring and a peach/violet/blue union, and it is deliberately not `aria-hidden`.
A whole fact row — the disc plus a title, a qualifier and the rule under it, as an `<li>`. That is `TrustFact`, which composes this at its defaults.

modules.summary: The hub grid: a set of cards, each of which is a whole link into a section of

usage.purpose: A hub grid where every card is a whole link into a section of the site: an icon, a heading, a line of description, supporting lines, and a call to action with an arrow. The card is the target, not the words at the bottom of it.
alsoFor: A card with no supporting lines, or none with an icon. Everything but the title and the href is optional, which is how the same grid serves a five-card index and a list of playbooks.
A next/link or any router link as the card root, rather than a bare anchor. Without one the caller nests an anchor inside an anchor, which is invalid and which no typechecker reports.
A hub whose cards are colour-coded by topic. The accent is a named union over tokens this package already ships, six neon and gold roles plus the brand peach.
watchFor: accent is a NAMED union, not a hex, and that is the point. The implementation this was extracted from took a free-form hex and one of its call sites passed the literal #fac089 against a brand peach of #fec089. One character, shipped, invisible to every gate because a raw hex in a styled-components prop is not a Tailwind arbitrary value. A union will not compile the typo.
Its fill is rgba(20,20,20,0.6), translucent so a textured page ground reads through. Overriding it with a chrome surface token makes it opaque and flattens the dither behind it.

linkAs, not asChild, and the difference is forced. asChild merges props into a single child and this component renders three of its own, so Slot throws React.Children.only. The first cut shipped asChild and the consumer's build failed prerendering on it.
notFor: A row that argues by contrast, costs then a gain. These cards are peers and none of them is making a claim about the others.
A row of tiles with one selected and a detail panel under it. Here every card carries its own detail and none is selected.

modules.summary: The integrations artifact: Skene Cloud's connections screen, drawn rather

usage.purpose: The integrations artifact: what Skene is attached to, and whether each connection is live.
alsoFor: Any connection or account list where the right-hand cell is a state — data sources, webhooks, installed apps.
A row whose supporting line is an identifier rather than a sentence, by passing a TagChip as the note — which is why `note` is a node.
An extra cell per row via `aside`, for a timestamp or a link.
watchFor: It is rows, not a table, and that is load-bearing at 390px: the left cell is prose of varying length and the right is a pill whose width is its word. A table column has one width for every row.
notFor: A real column contract with headers. That is DataTable.
Key/value reference data. That is KeyValueTable.

modules.summary: The homepage integrations band: cream copy column plus the four-card GSAP

usage.purpose: The homepage integrations band: cream copy column plus the four-card GSAP animation. Ported from skene-marketing-website's IntegrationsHighlight.
alsoFor: Custom CTAs via `actions`; pass outline `<Button>`s sized for a cream card.
A different texture behind the animation via `backgroundImage`.
watchFor: Composes `LightSectionCard` and `CardAnimationIntegrations`; the animation is client-only.
notFor: A generic cream band when you want different copy or a static visual instead of this animation.

modules.summary: A documented exception to `machine/rules.yaml`'s `styled_components_for_new_features`.

usage.purpose: Evidence, a traced journey step, and the PR review that catches it breaking, in one animated composition with a GTM/Engineering toggle. No props — content lives in named consts near the top of the source file, edited directly rather than passed in. Measures its own container width and switches between three hand-placed layouts (a three-panel row, a hero-column-width layout, a stacked phone layout) rather than using CSS breakpoints, because the same panel widths read differently depending on which parent gives it space.
alsoFor: Any `light`-classed container at any width, not just the `Bridge` band it originally shipped inside. It measures its own container and switches layout at 720px and 420px, which is what let skene-marketing-website drop it into a split hero's narrower right column as a second, real placement rather than a copy.
watchFor: Requires a `light` ancestor. Its tokens alias straight to this package's `--color-text-primary` etc., which default to the DARK reading (near-white) without one, and every card in the scene has a white/cream background regardless of page theme — without `light` somewhere above it, the ink text renders near-invisible on its own cards. `polarity: inherits` in the derived block below is why: this module sets no `light`/`dark` class itself, unlike a self-contained band such as `Bridge`.

The only styled-components module in the package (`documentation/20260825_journey_signal_scene_design.md` records why: a straight port of a component the founder already rejected rebuilding on package primitives once). Importing it does not pull styled-components into anything else, but do not use it as precedent for a second one — the exception is this component's history, not a reopened door.
notFor: A funnel or lifecycle strip with per-step status and no code/PR-review framing. This scene's Flows panel is a fixed three-row funnel illustrating the argument, not a general-purpose funnel primitive — for that, use `JourneyTrack`/`MiniFunnel`.

A PR review card on its own, outside the evidence-and-journey-step composition, or with different content than the built-in demo. This module has no props to swap the review's contents; `PrReview` is the standalone primitive for a review that needs its own data.

modules.summary: The journey track: the numbered steps of a funnel laid out as one line, each

usage.purpose: The numbered steps of a funnel on one line, where the connector between two steps is a gradient running from one step's status colour to the next's — the seam carries the state, not just the nodes. That is the section's argument, not a flourish: breakage happens *in the link* (an event that stops firing between checkout and confirmation), and the eye should find it before reading a label. The module also exports `MiniFunnel`, the small authored label/value/bar readout that usually sits beside the track.
alsoFor: Any three-state pipeline, not just a purchase funnel: onboarding checklists, deploy stages, data-source health. States are the fixed `good | warn | danger` triple bound to matcha/amber/red — the same vocabulary `Finding` uses — and `note` is free prose, so the domain lives entirely in the caller's copy.

Building your own layout from `JourneyStep`, which is exported separately. Its `index` prop is a `ReactNode` and `JourneyTrack` merely fills in the 1-based position, so rendering steps directly lets you pass a glyph (✓, ✕, an icon) or your own numbering into the ring.

Both orientations with no prop: the track is a stacked column below `md` and a row from `md` up, and the connector's gradient angle rides a `--journey-connector-angle` custom property specifically because an inline style cannot hold a media query. You get vertical and horizontal for free — but only that pairing; forcing one orientation means overriding classes.

Server rendering and animated composition. There is no `use client` and no internal state — state arrives as props — so a track that advances composes by re-rendering, and it drops into a server component without pulling a client boundary around its siblings.

`MiniFunnel` on its own, anywhere a small ranked readout helps: quota usage, share-of-total, step drop-off. Its bar width is routed through the `--mini-funnel-fill` custom property rather than set on `width` directly, which is the deliberate seam for a wrapper to transition or override it (grow-on-scroll, staged entrance) without this component owning any animation or state.

A verified or annotated track without composing steps by hand: each step's `glyph` replaces the ring's 1-based number (a ✓ on a proven step, per step, so a track can mix glyphed and numbered rings) while `JourneyTrack` still owns the connectors — the seam gradients keep deriving from the states with no re-derivation at the call site.
watchFor: The 34px ring size is hard-coded into the connector, not read from it: `ml-[17px]` stacked and `md:mt-[17px]` in a row are both half the ring. Resizing the ring via `JourneyStep`'s `className` leaves the connector aligned to the old centre.

This section owns no ground and carries no `light` / `dark` class of its own by design — every colour is a mode-aware role or derived from one, and nothing uses `chrome.text.*`. A caller putting it on a cream fill inside a dark page must put `light` on that band (rule 2), or `semantic.matcha` resolves to its dark value at 1.16:1 on cream.

The ring is `aria-hidden` and the label stays `text.primary` in *every* state — that is the rule the section exists to keep, not an oversight. So `note` is the only place the state is both announced and readable; a caller who omits it ships a broken step that only sighted readers can identify.

Two intentional non-obviousnesses that look like bugs: a `warn` end fades its connector to `surface.border` grey rather than contributing amber (an unmeasured step has no claim to make about the link), and `MiniFunnel`'s bars are `aria-hidden`, authored, and clamped 0-100 independently of `value` — the bar and the figure can disagree if the caller lets them.
notFor: A measured funnel chart. `MiniFunnel` has no axis and no scale, the widths are authored rather than computed, and its fill is `brand.peach` on purpose so quantities never borrow the status triple. For a shape-at-a-glance trend use `Sparkline`; for real numbers use a chart.

A progress indicator for a running job, or an interactive wizard. `PipelineStepper` owns the `done | active | pending` vocabulary and emphasises the active step; `JourneyTrack` has no active state, no state at all, and no click handling.

modules.summary: The reference table: a fixed set of columns, a fixed set of rows, and nothing

usage.purpose: The reference table: keys and values at two densities, with a masked value, a note and the 11px tag chip.
alsoFor: Any settings, environment or schema reference — the `reference` density drops the row fill and hover so it stops reading as a data grid.
A secret or token display via MaskedValue, which shows a prefix and a fixed number of dots.
Column-level formatting without touching cells: mono, muted, strong and nowrap are per-column flags.

The headerless key/value list — a settings readout whose column headings would only repeat what every row already says. `headerless` renders the same rows and column flags as a semantic `<dl>` (the term, then one `<dd>` per value column) rather than a table with visually hidden headers; the file header records why `sr-only` `<th>`s were rejected.
watchFor: TagChip is one of five names in this package for the same 11px mono tag. Prefer it, and do not add a sixth.
notFor: A found-things table with per-row status. That is DiscoveryTable.
An interactive product grid. That is ui/table.

modules.summary: The Lifecycle artifact: Skene Cloud's journey canvas, drawn rather than

usage.purpose: The lifecycle artifact: stages across the canvas, each holding milestones and the signals bound to them.
alsoFor: Any two-level map — phases and their steps, epics and their stories, a journey and its moments.
A single-level row of stages, by omitting milestones entirely.
Binding names as chips, since `bindings` is a list of nodes.
watchFor: It scrolls horizontally with a 190px column floor rather than wrapping, so a long lifecycle stays one canvas.
notFor: A single line of steps with a state-carrying connector. That is JourneyTrack.
Nodes joined by arrows with per-edge values. That is FlowDiagram.

modules.summary: The inverted section: one cream card carrying a whole section's worth of copy

usage.purpose: The inverted band: one cream card carrying a whole section's worth of copy — heading, italic promise, a ruled proof block, actions — with an optional visual panel opposite. It is `FeatureRow` at the other polarity, and its `light` root is a load-bearing accessibility mechanism, which is why the two were deliberately NOT collapsed behind a `tone` flag. SCOPE NARROWED IN 0.9.19: this is no longer a marketing section band. `render_marketing_cards_as_feature_row` gives that role to `FeatureRow` alone, because a page that alternates one repeating object cannot also alternate polarity without the cream band reading as a second system. What remains is every non-marketing use — product surfaces, gallery cases, and any dark-document context needing a correctly-inverted cream subtree, which is the part no other component does.
alsoFor: A closing CTA panel: `title` + `lede` + `actions`, no `visual` and no `children`. Without `visual` the grid stays single-column and you get a plain cream panel — `docs/sections.md` names this as the alternative to `FinalCta` when you want a panel rather than a full-bleed textured band.
Media-left layouts via `reverse`, which mirrors the grid with `md:col-start-*` / `md:row-start-1` on both columns rather than reordering the DOM (reading order stays copy-first).

Any node in `visual` — an image, a `ProductWindow` of either tone, a chart, an `AnnotatedCurve`. The column is `grid place-items-center` with no padding of its own and the root is `overflow-hidden`, so a full-bleed photo reaches the rounded edge and an inset one just pads the node you pass.

`children` is a free body slot, not a list API: a `<CheckList onLight>`, prose, a small table. It is given full column width on purpose (not a prose measure) so a CheckList's rules run the width of the column.
`actions` is a slot rather than a label/href pair, so it takes one button, two, or a button plus fine print — and lets you pick a variant that survives the inversion.

An eyebrowed band: `eyebrow` renders the package `Eyebrow` above the title with the on-cream overrides applied inside the card — the caller passes content, never colour, and cannot reintroduce the invisible-chrome-ink-on-cream trap the trust-panel story documents.
watchFor: `light` on the root is unconditional and first in the class list. Anything dark you nest has to re-assert `dark` itself: the gallery writes `<ProductWindow tone="dark" className="dark">`, because ProductWindow's dark branch sets `chrome.*` fills but adds no `dark` class of its own.

`brand.peach` inverts inside this card — #89684a, not #fec089 — so a default peach `<Button>` lands noticeably darker than the same button on the page around it. That is precisely why `actions` is a slot; pass the variant you actually want (the live section uses near-black buttons).

The horizontal rule and the whole lower block are gated on `hasProof = Boolean(children || actions)`. `title` + `lede` alone render a bare panel with no divider — that is deliberate (the rule can never appear with nothing under it), not a bug to patch.

The column ratios are hardcoded (`md:grid-cols-[1.1fr_0.9fr]`, mirrored to `[0.9fr_1.1fr]` when `reverse`), apply only at `md`+, and only when `visual` is passed. Below `md` it is one column, copy first, regardless of `reverse`.
notFor: The same copy-plus-visual shape on a dark page — use `FeatureRow`. It now shares the `lede` / `actions` names deliberately, and the two were kept separate rather than merged behind a `tone` prop because the polarity difference is the `light` mechanism, not a style.

A card inside a grid, or a small light frame around a mock. This is a whole band: a `<section>` with an `h2` at `clamp(2rem,3.2vw,3.25rem)` and 50px/46px vertical padding. For a light frame around a screenshot use `ProductWindow tone="light"`.

modules.summary: The proof strip: a heading, a stat line, a row of logo slots, and a caption

usage.purpose: The proof strip: a centred heading, a stat line, a row of outlined logo slots, and the caption that explains them. The slots are EMPTY by default and that is the component's argument, not a missing feature — the strip asserts that named proof only appears with consent, so a `LogoSlot` renders a child only when given one and no fabricated customer mark ever goes in a slot. Every colour is a mode-aware role, so the strip survives both the dark page and a cream `light` ancestor with no `onLight` prop.
alsoFor: A partially filled strip, honestly: pass fewer `LogoSlot` children than `count` and the remainder render as blanks, so a three-logo row keeps showing the two names it does not yet have.

`LogoSlot` on its own inside any grid you own — it is exported for the same reason `GlyphBadge` is, reachable without the strip around it, and a filled slot takes a `label` so the account is announced.
A bare mid-page divider row: omit `title` and `stat` and only the slots and caption render — nothing conditional leaves an empty heading block behind.
A strip whose filled logos should reach a screen reader: `decorative` defaults to true because five empty boxes say nothing, and flipping it false un-hides the row the day real logos land.
watchFor: `count` is also the column count from `sm` up, via a custom property on the grid. More children than `count` will wrap to a second line rather than being clipped, so keep the two in agreement.

The caption is a prop so no copy is baked in, but a strip without one is a row of unexplained boxes — the wireframes always ship it ("These slots stay empty until an account agrees to be named on-site."). Pass it.
notFor: A single figure beside a heading. That is a chip, not a band — this component earns its place only when the row of slots is the point.
A claim standing next to itemised, checkable facts. The proof strip gestures at accounts; the trust panel argues with evidence.

modules.summary: The MCP artifact's panels: a config snippet you are meant to paste, and the

usage.purpose: A panel inside the MCP artifact: a config snippet to paste, or the list of tools the server answers with.
alsoFor: Any code-plus-catalogue pairing — an API key block and its scopes, a config and its options.
A tool or endpoint list on its own, via McpTool rows inside a titled block.
watchFor: It is one panel, not the window. The surface it depicts stacks two of these inside a single AppWindow, which is why there is no crumb prop here.
The code block takes themed tokens rather than chrome, because it is a settings screen and not a terminal.
notFor: A terminal transcript with traffic lights. That is patterns/terminal.
An install snippet with a copy button. That is TerminalBlock.

modules.summary: A full-bleed advisory bar across the top of a page.

usage.purpose: A full-bleed advisory bar across the top of a page, carrying one line: this page is archived, this content is from an earlier version, this environment is staging. It spans the viewport, sits above the content, and separates itself with a single hairline.
alsoFor: A status or alert bar rather than an advisory. The landmark role is a prop, so the same bar can announce assertively when the message actually warrants interrupting a screen reader.
watchFor: It is NOT Alert and cannot be swapped for one. Alert is an inset card with a title and a description that sits in the content, bordered on four sides and inside the page's measure. This spans the viewport and sits above it. Reaching for Alert here produces a rounded box floating where a bar belongs.

Its ground is translucent, rgba(255,255,255,0.04), so the textured header underneath shows through. Overriding it with a chrome surface token makes it opaque and punches a flat rectangle through the dither.
notFor: An inset callout inside the content, bordered on four sides and inside the page's measure. This spans the viewport and sits above it.

modules.summary: The workspace Overview: a row of small tiles, each a caption, one number and a

usage.purpose: The workspace overview: a row of small tiles, each a caption, one number and what the number is made of.
alsoFor: Any set of commensurable counts — four numbers that belong in one sweep. A tile that styled itself differently would read as the important one.
A ratio or a word instead of a count, since `value` is a node: 2 / 1 / 0 / 0 and On are both valid.
watchFor: Its tile is byte-identical to CheckResult in evaluator-check — same root class string, same grid recipe at a different floor.
notFor: One number as the subject of a whole panel. That is MetricCard.
A single fact beside a heading. That is StatChip.

modules.summary: The progress pipeline shown inside a product window while a long job runs.

usage.purpose: A labelled progress track: N steps with state rings, joined by connectors the STEPPER owns and fills from the state of the step on their left, above an optional title/subtitle. It was built for a long job running inside a light `ProductWindow`, and two decisions carry that job — connectors are derived rather than drawn per-step, so N dots read as one track filling left to right; and emphasis runs backwards from instinct, with the ACTIVE step taking the label weight and a peach halo while done steps recede to matcha, because a running job's question is "what is it doing now", not "what has it finished".
alsoFor: Any step count and any mix of states — `steps` is a plain array and connectors are derived (N-1), so a five-step onboarding checklist or a two-step form indicator works unchanged.

Dark grounds via `onLight={false}`. The flag switches only the hairline token (`chrome.line.subtle` instead of `chrome.line.onLight`); everything legible already uses the theme-aware `text.*` role and follows a `light`/`dark` ancestor. Be aware the gallery case deliberately covers only the light path, so the dark rendering is supported by props but has no visual snapshot behind it.

A static "how it works" or completed-summary readout: `icon` per step replaces the ✓/dot with a number or glyph, and setting every step to `done` (or every step to `pending`) gives a finished or not-yet-started outline rather than a live job.
A bare track with no header: omit `title` and `subtitle` and only the `<ol>` renders (the `mt-5` is conditional), so it drops under a heading you own or into a card you already have.
`PipelineStep` is exported separately for a single-step readout — though standalone steps get no connectors, which is the whole reason the array API exists.
watchFor: `aria-current="step"` on the active step is the ONLY state exposed to assistive tech; the rings and glyphs are `aria-hidden` on purpose. Nothing is enforced, so two `active` steps emit two `aria-current="step"`, and `done` vs `pending` is invisible to a screen reader — if completion must be announced, it has to be in the `label`.
The connector reads only the LEFT step's state, so an out-of-order array renders literally: a `done` after a `pending` draws a filled matcha rule leading into a hollow ring.

The geometry is hand-computed and interlocking: a fixed 38px ring, and connector offsets of `ml-[18px]` (stacked) and `sm:mt-[18px]` (row) that are exactly its centre. Change the ring size and the track stops aligning with the rings. Steps also cap at `sm:max-w-[160px]`.

The breakpoint is `sm`, not `md` (the header notes three labelled steps need roughly 390px), and the root padding is a fixed `p-[22px]` sized for a ProductWindow body — both are worth re-checking if you drop this into a narrower or differently-padded container.
notFor: A funnel or journey diagram where each step carries health rather than progress — use `JourneyTrack`, whose connector is a gradient between the two states it joins so a break reads as happening in the link. PipelineStepper's connector is binary filled/not and its vocabulary is done/active/pending.

A self-advancing progress indicator. There is no `use client`, no timer, no internal state — deliberately, so the file stays server-renderable. Animating it means the parent owns the state and re-renders with new `steps`.

modules.summary: Pricing: the grid and the tier card. The monthly/yearly switch is the only

usage.purpose: A pricing tier card plus the grid that holds a row of them (`PlanGrid` + `PlanCard`). It is pure markup — no state, no client directive — because the only interactive part of a pricing section, the billing switch, was deliberately split into `billing-toggle.tsx` so this file stays server-renderable. The shape's real argument is comparison-by-inversion: `featured` flips one card to cream-on-dark, lifts it `md:-translate-y-3`, and drops a `--shadow-modal` on it, so a row of peers stops reading as peers and one of them becomes the recommendation.
alsoFor: A billing/subscription panel in a product surface: `flag="Current plan"`, `bestFor={{label: 'Renews', value: 'Sep 12'}}` as a generic labelled metadata block, `action` as a Manage button, `footnote` for the fine print.

Non-currency tiers. `price` is a `ReactNode` rendered in a `<strong>`, so "Free", "Custom", or "Let's talk" work as-is, and `unit` takes "/seat", "/yr", "per repo" — nothing in the component knows it is money.

Non-pricing package or offer cards — service tiers, plan-shaped feature bundles. `features` is an untyped `ReactNode` slot, so a `<dl>`, a `<Table>`, or plain paragraphs go in where the demo puts a `<CheckList>`.

Grids other than three-across. `PlanGrid` merges `className` through `cn` (clsx + tailwind-merge), so `md:grid-cols-2` or `lg:grid-cols-4` genuinely replaces the base `md:grid-cols-3` rather than fighting it.
Highlighting one item in any set of sibling cards — `featured` carries no pricing semantics, only the cream inversion and the lift.

The featured promotion on a CREAM ground: `featuredTone="dark"` inverts the card to the invariant near-black fill with the `dark` class pinning every mode-aware token in the subtree, same lift and `--shadow-modal` — because the default cream inversion is cream-on-cream inside a light panel. A nested `CheckList` then wants its default rendering, not `onLight`.
watchFor: `featured` applies the `light` class, and that is load-bearing, not decoration (sections.md rule 2). Anything you pass into `features`/`action`/`bestFor` must use the theme-aware `text.*` role; `chrome.text.*` is invariant and renders cream on the cream card, i.e. invisible. When `featured`, also pass `onLight` to a nested `CheckList`.
The tier marker is hardcoded `<Chip tone="neutral">` — no prop reaches it. A healthy/live-toned tier marker needs one small prop addition (e.g. `tierTone?: ChipTone` forwarded to `Chip`).

The featured shadow is an inline `style={{ boxShadow: 'var(--shadow-modal)' }}`, so a `shadow-*` utility in `className` loses to it. Same for `bestFor`'s border colour, set inline from `--color-chrome-line-on-light`.

`PlanGrid` uses `items-start` on purpose: a stretched grid would re-equalise row height and cancel the featured card's `-translate-y-3`. Overriding to `items-stretch` silently kills the lift. Cards are held level by `min-h-[420px]` instead.
The price renders at `clamp(2.55rem, 4vw, 4rem)`. Long strings ("Contact sales", "$1,299/mo") wrap or crowd the `unit` at that size.
notFor: A feature-by-feature comparison matrix across tiers — the card has no cell/row model. Use `sections/comparison-table` (`ComparisonTable`, `ComparisonRow`, `TableCheck`, `TableDash`); it is a deep import, not in the root barrel.

A generic content card or dashboard tile. The tier chip, oversized price and 420px floor are all pricing furniture — use `ui/card` for product surfaces, or `LightSectionCard` for a cream editorial panel.

modules.summary: The GitHub pull-request review artifact: the bot's comment on a PR, drawn

usage.purpose: The pull-request artifact: Skene's review on a PR, with findings by severity, a suggested fix and the file it lands in.
alsoFor: Any review or audit output with ranked findings — a linter run, a security scan, a code review.
A passing review with no findings at all, via `status` and an empty issues list.
watchFor: Severity maps high/medium/low onto the same three semantic colours as every other status vocabulary in the package, under a fourth set of names.
Its author badge is StatPill minus the dot, hand-rolled in a file that already imports StatPill eight lines earlier.
notFor: The diff itself rather than the review around it. That is SideBySideDiff.
A single measured finding on a marketing band. That is Finding.

modules.summary: The framed product mock: a customer's dashboard rendered inside a marketing

usage.purpose: The chrome that frames a product mock inside a marketing section: rounded border, modal shadow, and an optional title bar with a left title and a right `status` slot. Its default `tone="light"` is the argument rather than a style choice — the page around it is Skene's dark chrome, so the thing inside the frame reads as the customer's own tool; a dark window on a dark page reads as a screenshot of Skene itself. Ships alongside `WindowStatus` (the title bar's chip), `WindowToolbar` (a filter/breadcrumb strip) and `WindowChip`.
alsoFor: The deliberate opposite reading: `tone="dark"` frames Skene's own surfaces (MCP output, a tracking plan, a CLI-adjacent view) on `chrome.surface.1`, and it is the mode `WindowToolbar` and `WindowChip` were built for.
