Framing anything, not just a dashboard: `children` renders raw under the title bar, so `PipelineStepper`, a `Finding` list, a screenshot `` or a table all fit — the gallery's `section-pipeline-stepper` case does exactly this.

A chromeless light island: omit both `title` and `status` and the whole header block does not render, leaving a cream, `light`-scoped, shadowed panel for when you need light-on-dark inversion smaller than a full `LightSectionCard`.

Any title-bar state marker: `status` is a ReactNode slot, and `WindowStatus` covers the two readings a window frame can express — default `healthy` (matcha) and `live` (violet) — while forwarding `className` merged last, so a caller's utility wins.
Standalone use outside a feature row: nothing couples it to `FeatureRow`; it is a self-contained `max-w-[640px]` block and the gallery renders it directly.
watchFor: `tone="light"` puts the `light` class on the root and that is load-bearing, not decoration: without it every mode-aware token inside — `semantic.matcha`, `errorRed`, `brand.peach` — resolves to its DARK value against the cream fill (matcha #d7f4ab on #faf1e9 is 1.16:1). It also inverts whatever you pass as `children`, so a default peach `Button` lands much darker in here than on the page.

`WindowToolbar` is a dark-window part despite living in this file: it hardcodes `border-chrome-line-subtle` and `text-chrome-text-muted-warm`, both invariant dark-surface tokens, so inside a light window the rule is near-invisible and the text colour is wrong. The window's own internal rules correctly switch to `chrome.line.onLight`.
`max-w-[640px]` is a class and can be overridden through `className` (cn is twMerge), but `boxShadow: var(--shadow-modal)` is an inline style and no class will beat it.

Nesting `tone="dark"` inside a `light` ancestor needs `className="dark"` to pin it — the gallery does this for the dark window inside `LightSectionCard`, because otherwise the light ancestor pins that window's mode-aware tokens to their light values in both page modes.

`WindowStatus` deliberately overrides the shared `Chip`'s `tracking-[0.08em]` back to `0.05em` to preserve its browser-verified rendering. If you touch chip geometry expecting one value everywhere, this is the declared exception.
notFor: Code, CLI output or a diff — that is `Terminal` (monospace, traffic lights). components.yaml states the two read as different objects on purpose and should not be substituted.
A whole cream section band carrying copy and buttons. This is a frame with a 640px cap and no title/lede/actions slots; use `LightSectionCard`.

modules.summary: The question grid: a row of cards, each one a category tag over a question the

usage.purpose: A 1–4 column grid of near-empty cards, each one a mono category `tag` sitting at the top of the card with a question (or claim) below it and an optional answer. The card is deliberately a border, a 14px radius and a peach corner glow with no opaque fill — that is what lets it sit on a dark band or a cream one without needing a polarity class or a token audit. It exists for the "here is what you'll actually be able to answer" band, where the copy does all the work and the container must not compete with it.
alsoFor: An FAQ or objection-handling teaser band: `tag` as the category ("BILLING", "OBJECTION"), `title` as the question, `children` as the short answer. Static only — see notFor.
A use-case or persona grid: `tag` as the audience ("FOR ENGINEERS"), `title` as the outcome. Same three slots, no change.

A 2-up or 4-up feature grid via the `columns` prop. `columns={4}` is not simply four across — the static map gives `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`, which is the sensible ladder for four short cards.
A single full-width statement card with `columns={1}` — though the fixed 58px tag gap and `min-h` were tuned for a ~270px-wide card and will read as a lot of air at full bleed.

Clickable cards, by wrapping each `QuestionCard` in the caller's own `<a>`/`<Link>`. `className` is forwarded to the `<article>`, so hover/focus styling can be supplied from outside — but the component ships no interactive affordance of its own.
watchFor: The `mb-[58px]` under the tag is a fixed margin, not `mt-auto`, and it is load-bearing: it is what makes the tag read as a label on the card rather than a kicker on the sentence, and what keeps every tag on one baseline across the row. It only works because the grid's default `items-stretch` gives the cards a shared row height — drop these into a flex row, or pass `items-start`, and the alignment goes.

Omitting `tag` removes the 58px with it, so the question floats at the top of a card still held open by `min-h-[230px] md:min-h-[270px]` — a visible void underneath. The card is designed to be tagged.

The tag colour is hardcoded `text-brand-peach`; there is no per-card accent. Colour-coding categories would need a small prop addition — a `tone`/`accent` prop feeding the tag's colour, mirroring `ValueCard`'s `TONE_ACCENT` map.

`COLUMN_CLASS` is a static 1|2|3|4 map because Tailwind cannot see an interpolated class name. Five or six columns is a compile error, not a runtime surprise — and fixing it means adding a map entry, not passing a number through.

Adding a background fill via `className` works (the corner glow is `backgroundImage`, a different property) but it is exactly the change the file header warns against: a filled card acquires its own ground, at which point it needs a `light`/`dark` class and every token inside it needs re-checking.
notFor: A real FAQ accordion. There is no disclosure behaviour and no `use client` — this is props in, markup out. Use `ui/accordion`.
A stats or metrics band. The fixed tag gap and min-height are tuned for one line of question plus a sentence; a number and a unit leave the card mostly empty. Use `StatChip` or `ValueCards`.

modules.summary: The proposal: what Skene suggests doing next, and what makes it worth doing.

usage.purpose: The proposal: what to do next, and what makes it worth doing. Deliberately without a status colour.
alsoFor: Any suggestion block — a next step, a recommended setting, an upsell that should not look like an alert.
Qualifier chips under the body, via `meta`, which takes nodes so TagChip fits.
watchFor: It carries no status colour on purpose. An amber pill on a suggestion teaches a reader who has learned that amber means drift to read the suggestion as a fault.
Its fill and hairline mix from currentColor, so it works on the light window it shipped in and on the dark page with no prop.
notFor: A measured state. That is Finding, which owns the status vocabulary.
A verdict spoken by the product. That is AgentCallout — the same padding and eyebrow spec in a different voice.

modules.summary: The audit score: a partial arc on a track, with the value inside it.

usage.purpose: A score against a scale: a partial arc on a track with the value inside it.
alsoFor: Any bounded score — coverage, health, completeness, a readiness percentage.
At any size, since the digits are sized from the ring: one prop moves the whole figure.
watchFor: `status` binds the reserved good | warn | danger vocabulary and never peach: peach is the action colour, so a peach fault reads as a call to action.
The default is warn, not good, so a forgotten prop cannot paint a failing score in the reassurance colour.
`label` is required because the visible digits are aria-hidden — it is the accessible name, not decoration.
notFor: A determinate bar on a product surface. That is ui/progress.
A number with a delta and a sparkline rather than a scale. That is MetricCard.

modules.summary: The halftone field a product mock sits on inside a feature row.

usage.purpose: The halftone field a panel floats on: a container that paints one of the three real site textures (`card1/2/3_bg.webp`) and insets its child by a percentage of the track width. The percentage is the whole design — the live panel is 84–92% of its container, and only a percentage holds that proportion at every width; a fixed padding turns the field into a coloured border on a short wide card. It is the narrowest of the package's four texture tools: field behind a mock inside a feature row, as opposed to `HeroBackdrop` (hero strip), `DitheredMedia` (whole hero composition) and `DitherOverlay` (the raw layer).
alsoFor: Standalone use outside a feature row — the gallery's `section-backdrop` case renders three of them in a plain grid wrapping an arbitrary card, so any node can be the floating panel.
Consumer artwork: `src` takes any URL and overrides `texture`, which is the supported path for a page-specific image or for a consumer that does not have Skene's assets.
Retuning the float: `inset` is a plain number in percent (default 6) — raise it to make a small panel sit deeper in the field, lower it toward 0 for a near-full-bleed texture edge.

Choosing a field by subject: `texture` is `journey | github | schema` and the pairing is semantic, not a tint picker (journeys/funnels/measurement, GitHub/PRs/editor chrome, schema/connections/keys), so a reader who knows the live site meets the same backdrop behind the same kind of thing.
Shape and fill control via `className`, which merges onto the root — `rounded-xl` in the gallery, `h-full w-full` in how `FeatureRow` embeds it.
watchFor: `minHeight: '22rem'` is set as an **inline style** and there is no `style` prop on `SectionBackdropProps`, so no Tailwind `min-h-*` in `className` can beat it — inline styles win and twMerge cannot reach them. Making it shorter needs one small prop addition to this file (a `minHeight` or a passthrough `style` prop); say so rather than fighting it from the call site.

`padding: ${inset}%` applies to all four sides, and CSS resolves percentage padding against the container's **width** in both axes — so a wide, short container gets large vertical padding from a small `inset`. The 22rem floor exists because without vertical room the texture only shows left and right, which is the border failure again in the other axis.

Children are flex items on a `flex items-center` root, not layers: exactly one node goes in the `relative w-full` z-1 wrapper. And there is no overlay element in this file — the texture is a CSS `background-image` on the container itself, so the header comment's "aria-hidden, pointer-events-none" describes `FeatureRow`'s sheen, not anything here to restyle.

Texture URLs are resolved with `new URL('../../assets/…', import.meta.url)` on purpose, so a bundler rewrites them and consumers need not copy files into their own `public/`. That assumes a bundler that handles `import.meta.url` asset references; unbundled Node resolution yields a `file://` path.
notFor: A hero. Use `DitheredMedia` for a full hero composition or `HeroBackdrop` for a dark strip fading into the page — this component's 22rem floor and percentage inset are sized for a panel inside a row.
A plain tinted or gradient panel. It always loads a raster texture; use a div with a token background, or `DitherOverlay` if you want only the dither layer over your own stack.

modules.summary: The two-column diff: what the coding agent wrote beside what the check

usage.purpose: Two columns of code with added and removed lines marked — what was written beside what was expected.
alsoFor: Any before/after code comparison — a migration, a suggested fix, a config change.
A single column of annotated code, by rendering one DiffColumn.
Localised or relabelled markers via `addedLabel` and `removedLabel`.
watchFor: It applies `dark` to itself: the diff is GitHub chrome and stays dark on a light page, which is what the vendor tokens are for.
Its column header is byte-identical to ArtPanel's bar, in a file that does not import it.
notFor: The review around a diff — author, findings, fix. That is PrReview.
A plain code block with no diff semantics. That is McpCode.

modules.summary: The two small labels that recur beside headings: a fact, and a promise.

usage.purpose: Two small pills that sit beside headings: `StatChip` asserts something true right now ("121 stars"), `MetaChip` marks something not shipped yet (prose, a hairline divider, then a peach status word). They are two components rather than one with a `variant` precisely so a forgotten prop can never turn a roadmap item into a live claim about the product — two names cannot be defaulted into each other. Both derive their border and fill from `currentColor` via `color-mix`, which is what lets one chip survive both the dark page and the cream `LightSectionCard` with no `onLight` prop.
alsoFor: Recolouring the entire chip by setting only the text colour. Because border (26%/22%) and fill (7%/6%) are `color-mix` on `currentColor`, passing e.g. `className="text-semantic-matcha"` retints border, fill, and type together. That `currentColor` derivation IS the tone mechanism — there is no `tone` prop and none is needed.

`MetaChip` as a general "description · marker" chip. `status` is a `ReactNode`, not an enum — BETA, SOON, DEPRECATED, `v2.1`, a region code — rendered monospace, uppercased, tracked at 0.07em. The divider is a real 13px element rather than a `│` glyph, so it tracks the chip height whatever you put on either side.

Any leading mark, not just the shipped emoji. The `icon` slot is a `ReactNode` with `shrink-0`, so a small inline SVG or a coloured status dot drops in — but it is `aria-hidden`, so the visible text has to carry the whole meaning.

Composed content in `children` (also a `ReactNode`): a `<strong>` figure with a muted trailing word, a linked count, a short unit. Both chips are `inline-flex` `<span>`s, so they flow in prose and wrap cleanly in a `flex flex-wrap gap-3` row — the shape the gallery uses.

Dropping onto a cream surface unchanged. The type uses the mode-aware `text-muted-strong` / `text-muted` roles, so a `light` ancestor inverts everything including the derived edges. No variant, no second call site.
watchFor: The border and background are inline `style` rules, so a `border-*` or `bg-*` utility passed via `className` loses to them. Change the colour by changing the text colour, not the border colour.

`MetaChip`'s status word is hardcoded `text-brand-peach` — it is the one part NOT derived from `currentColor`. Retinting the chip leaves the status peach, which is usually right and occasionally a surprise.

Never reach for `chrome.*` here. `chrome.text.*` is invariant cream by definition, and these chips render on cream; the whole colour scheme (including the derived edges) is built on the theme-aware `text.*` role for that reason. There is no mode-aware line token, which is exactly why the edges are derived rather than tokenised.

Geometry is `rounded-full`, 12px, non-mono — deliberately NOT the 10px mono rectangle of `Chip`/`WindowStatus`. `docs/sections.md` §2 point 3 records this as an open decision (adopt the window-chip geometry or justify the pill), so do not quietly "harmonise" one side of it.
notFor: Product-surface state. These are section furniture next to headings; for a status marker in a UI use `Badge` (the shadcn primitive) or `Chip` / `WindowStatus` for the 10px mono rectangle.
A section-heading kicker. That is `Eyebrow` (pattern), which owns the `font.tracking.eyebrow` token — a different job at a different tracking.

modules.summary: The four-ways-in grid: a small set of peer cards on a textured field, one of

usage.purpose: A compact grid of peer cards on a textured field, one of them drawn cream, where every card carries its own detail: the “ways in” band, four surfaces two across.
alsoFor: Any two-to-four item set of alternatives where one is editorially led — entry points, plans, channels. Nothing in it is homepage-specific.
Which cell is the cream one is the caller's, so the lit card can follow the page's argument instead of always being the first.
A plain panel with no artwork behind it, by omitting the texture — the grid does not depend on the field.
A command or endpoint per card, as a mono chip whose hairline is mixed from the card's own ink so it holds on the cream cell and the ink ones alike.
watchFor: The featured card carries `light` and the other cards carry `dark`, and both are load-bearing. Without them a mode-aware token keeps the wrong value — `text.primary` resolves to #faf1e9 on a #faf1e9 fill, which is not dim, it is absent.
The chip reads as tested, which is exactly why it is optional. Pass one only where the exact string is verifiable in a source; an absent chip is not a hole in the design.
The glyph is a character, never a named HTML entity. JSX entity tables are per-compiler and `machine/rules.yaml` bans them outright.
The grid is literally two across at `sm` and one below it, not `auto-fit`. Four tracks in a ~640px band give each card 139px, and every two-word title wraps.
notFor: A row of tiles with ONE panel under it explaining whichever tile is chosen. That is `SurfaceTiles` with `SurfaceDetail` as a sibling. Use that when one surface is being explained, and this when all of them are, each in its own card.
Cards that argue by contrast — N of them naming what the situation costs, then one naming what it becomes. These cards are peers; the tone here marks the lit one rather than turning the argument.

A whole band: a copy column beside a visual panel, at band scale. Its copy column alone carries 38.4px of side padding, wider than the content a 223px cell holds. This grid is what goes IN a FeatureRow's visual, not a nest of four more.

modules.summary: The surfaces Skene runs on, as a row of tiles — and the panel that explains

usage.purpose: The surfaces a product runs on, as a row of tiles with one picked out, and the panel that explains the chosen one.
alsoFor: Any set of options where one is editorially highlighted — plans, integrations, entry points.
A command or identifier under the row, via SurfaceDetail's `code`, which renders a mono chip rather than a terminal.
Tinted icons per tile through `accent`, which reuses FeatureIcon's vocabulary plus a neutral.
watchFor: `selected` carries the `light` class, which is the whole mechanism. Without it, cream type lands on a cream fill — the bug that shipped invisible twice in this package.
Selection is presentational. There is no onSelect and no internal state, so a real picker means the caller owns the state.
notFor: Commensurable numbers rather than choices. That is OverviewTiles, where nothing can be selected.
Options that each need a price, a feature list and a CTA. That is PlanCard.

modules.summary: The person card for the about page: a name, a role, and optionally a

usage.purpose: The about-page person card and its grid: a name as a heading, a role in the small-caps monospace register, an optional bio/links block, and an optional square media frame that only exists when media does. The card is designed for the no-photo state — type on a bordered panel that looks finished — so a team page needs no photographer and no stock placeholder. Cards are `<li>`s and `TeamGrid` is the `<ul>`, the same peers-in-a-list argument `TrustPanel` makes for its facts.
alsoFor: Any person-shaped entry, not only employees: advisors, authors on a contributors page, speakers — `name` and `role` are slots and no copy is baked in.
A card with links: anchors passed in `children` are styled here (underline, offset, hover to `text.primary`), so a bare `<a href>` at the call site is already visible.
An illustration or monogram instead of a photo — `media` is a `ReactNode` slot, not a `src`, and the frame's sizing rules make whatever is passed fill it without call-site styling.
A grid that IS the section: `as` moves the name heading to `h2` when no section heading sits above the stack.
watchFor: `TeamGrid`'s slot renders inside a `<ul>`, so pass `TeamCard`s, not arbitrary markup — a free-floating `<div>` child is invalid list nesting the browser will repair for you, wrongly.
`alt` on a portrait is the caller's job, and beside the printed name it is usually `alt=""` — the media slot cannot know what it is handed.
notFor: A fact with a qualifier in a stack — the icon-title-body row on cream. A person is not a fact and the card carries its own surface.
A benefit or capability tile. If the "person" is really a role description with no name, it is a value card wearing a face.

modules.summary: The install block: a terminal frame holding one or more shell lines, each with

usage.purpose: The install block: a terminal frame holding one or more shell lines, each with its own copy button.
alsoFor: Any copyable command list — install steps, a CLI walkthrough, a set of environment exports.
Output lines that are not copyable, by setting `copyable` false — which is how a transcript mixes commands and results.
A different visible string from what is copied, via `display` against `command`.
watchFor: It is the client boundary and is deliberately absent from the root barrel: a use client directive on a re-exported module poisons the barrel for server rendering, which package-contract asserts against. Deep-import it.
It draws the terminal frame itself rather than using the skene-terminal class in effects.css, so it does not match patterns/terminal — 12px radius against 8px.
notFor: A transcript with no copy affordance. That is patterns/terminal.
A config block to read rather than run. That is McpCode.

modules.summary: The window furniture: three 10px dots, red then yellow then green.

usage.purpose: The three window-chrome dots — red, yellow, green, 10px each — as one `aria-hidden` group at an 8px gap. It exists so a shell bar, an editor header or a GitHub file header can carry window furniture without hand-rolling three spans, which is what five files were doing: `TerminalBlock` and `PrReview` in this package, and two skene-site routes that each declared a local copy plus a comment saying the fix belonged upstream.
alsoFor: Any drawn window header, not only a shell — an editor chrome bar, a browser mock, a GitHub file header. It carries no terminal semantics at all: it is three coloured circles in a flex row, and it needs no parent and no context.
A roomier bar, by passing `gap-*` — `cn` treats it as a `gap` conflict so the caller's value wins. That is how `PrReview` gets GitHub's 12px against the terminal bar's 8px, from the same component.
watchFor: `className` lands on the WRAPPER. The three dots take invariant `terminal-chrome.traffic.*` tokens and are not reachable from outside — a recolourable red light is not a variant.

`patterns/terminal` draws the same three dots and does NOT use this: they are a `::before` with two box-shadows on `.skene-terminal` in `styles/effects.css`. A `Terminal` therefore has its lights whether or not you render this, and rendering both gives six. Which of the two terminals wins is the open `terminals` decision, and this component does not settle it.
There is no `size` prop. 10px is what both call sites shipped and what the CSS half draws; a fourth diameter would push the two terminals further apart rather than closer.
notFor: Saying something. These are furniture and carry no state; a dot that means a state, with the word beside it, is `StatPill`, which binds bad | warn | ok to the semantic colours.
A whole terminal frame. `patterns/terminal` already paints its own lights in CSS — reach for this only when you are building the bar yourself.

modules.summary: The trust panel: a cream card split in two — the claim on the left, the facts

usage.purpose: A cream panel split into a claim and its evidence: heading, lede and a row of links on the left, a stack of `TrustFact` items on a deeper cream to the right. The split is the argument — the reassurance is not a paragraph asserting itself but a paragraph standing next to checkable facts, which is why the evidence track is the wider of the two (`0.9fr 1.1fr`). It is a fixed-polarity object: the root carries `light` unconditionally, so it is a cream card on a dark page, with a peach bloom rising from the bottom-left corner that the token system gets right on cream for free.
alsoFor: Any claim-plus-itemised-proof panel, not just security: "what's included", "how it works", "what we do with your data". `title` + `lede` + `TrustFact`s is the shape, and no copy is baked in.

A single-column cream statement or CTA panel — omit `children` and the `md:grid-cols-[0.9fr_1.1fr]` template is not applied at all. That collapse is an explicit design decision in the source, not an accident.
A legal/footnote band: the `links` slot is a wrapped flex row that styles whatever anchors you pass (`underline`, `underline-offset-4`, hover to `text.primary`) without owning their hrefs or labels.
A plan-inclusions panel, using each `TrustFact`'s 38px `icon` circle for a check glyph and `children` for the limit or caveat.

`TrustFact` on its own inside any `<ul>` you own — it is exported, it is a self-contained `<li>` that draws its own separating rule, and it needs no context from `TrustPanel`. Cream surfaces only (see watchFor).

A fact row on a dark band: `TrustFact tone="muted"` swaps the row's two invariant pieces of on-light chrome — the separating rule and the disc — for their theme-following pair (`border`, `GlyphBadge tone="muted"`), so the stack is legible outside the cream panel while the default `tint` rendering inside it is untouched.
watchFor: `light` is unconditional and first in the class list. There is no dark variant and you cannot make one by overriding `className` — `bg-brand-light` is an invariant cream, and every mode-aware token in the subtree has already resolved for a cream ground.

`TrustFact`'s hairlines and its icon circle's border are `chrome-line-on-light` — an invariant dark rule at 14% designed for cream. Lifted onto a dark surface those rules and that circle are effectively invisible. The doc comment calls this out as the one deliberate exception to the theme-aware-tokens rule. Since 0.11.0 that is what `TrustFact`'s `tone="muted"` exists for — the theme-following pair for any other ground.

`children` renders directly inside the `<ul>` (chosen over an inner wrapper specifically to avoid `display: contents`, which several browsers still strip list semantics from). Pass `TrustFact`s, i.e. `<li>`s — a `<div>` or a wrapper component breaks the "3 of 5" a screen reader would otherwise give.

The fact separators live on the item (`border-b … first:pt-0 last:border-b-0 last:pb-0`), not on a divider element, so the stack must not also be spaced by a parent `gap` — that double-spaces the rhythm. The icon circle also renders when `icon` is absent, on purpose, to keep every title's left edge aligned.

`title` is capped at `max-w-[440px]` and `lede` at `max-w-[430px]`, and the glow is absolutely positioned inside the left cell only. Long copy will not fill the column, and the bloom never reaches the facts panel.
notFor: A generic two-column band. Its polarity is fixed cream; for a dark band with copy on one side use `FeatureRow`, and for a cream one whose second track is a visual use `LightSectionCard` (its `visual` slot is what the facts column is not — the right track here is a `<ul>`).
Comparing facts across options. The facts are a single stack of peers with no column axis; that is `ComparisonTable`.

The 38px disc on its own, without the rule, the 22px rhythm and the qualifier slot a fact row brings. `TrustFact` composes `GlyphBadge` at its defaults, so a row that only wants the circle — at 38px or at 32 — should take the badge directly.

modules.summary: The value band: a row of cards that argues by CONTRAST. A stack of cards

usage.purpose: A responsive card band whose argument is carried by tone rather than by copy: N cards stating what the current situation costs, then one stating what it becomes. `ValueCard` takes a mono `label`, a `title` line and an optional body, and the `tone` union (`'cost' | 'gain'`) is the only thing that moves — `cost` borrows `semantic.errorRed` for the label and a neutral 14% hairline, `gain` takes `brand.peach` with a 34% border and a left-to-right directional wash so the last card reads as an arrival rather than one more tile. It exists so a band can make a turn; a row of identically-weighted cards degrades into a feature list and says nothing.
alsoFor: Any before/after or problem/payoff band: `label` is free text, so "BEFORE"/"AFTER", "TODAY"/"WITH SKENE", "MANUAL"/"AUTOMATED" all work with no code change — only `tone` decides the colour.

A risk or defect summary where every card is a `cost`: `tone` defaults to `'cost'`, so a stack of audit findings needs only `label` + `title` + body. (For a measured, instrumented state use `Finding` instead — see notFor.)

A plain neutral card grid: omit `label` entirely and leave `tone` at its default. With no label there is no accent on screen at all — you get a 14px-radius card, a 1.8% wash and a near-invisible hairline, i.e. a generic content card.

`ValueCards` on its own as a bare auto-fit grid wrapper. `children` is typed `React.ReactNode`, not `ValueCard[]`, so it will lay out any children at `repeat(auto-fit,minmax(240px,1fr))` from `md` up, single column below.
A three-tier emphasis band, by mixing labelled `cost` cards with unlabelled default cards and one `gain` — no third tone needed, because the label's presence is itself an axis.

A row of labelled flat peers: `tone="neutral"` keeps the mono kicker but takes `text.muted` for it and claims neither a defect nor a payoff — three use-case cards can carry labels without any of them reading as a cost, and mixing one `gain` back in restores the turn.
watchFor: `tone` defaults to `'cost'`. That is deliberate (costs are the majority of the band) but it means a forgotten `tone` renders a red label, not a neutral one.

The accent lands via inline `style={{ color: accent }}` on the label and inline `borderColor`/`backgroundImage` on the `<article>`. A `text-*` or `border-*` utility passed through `className` will not win against those; to retint, add a tone member to `TONE_ACCENT` rather than fighting it from the call site.

`ValueCards` deliberately carries no `light`/`dark` class — everything is derived from the mode-aware `text.primary` and `brand.peach`, so it inherits polarity. Per rule 2 in docs/sections.md, a caller putting this band on a cream panel inside a dark page still owes that panel its own `light` class, or the 1.8% wash and the hairline resolve to their dark values against cream.

The `gain` wash is directional — `linear-gradient(90deg, …, transparent 62%)` — and knows nothing about position. It always enters from the left edge, which reads as arrival only when the gain card is last in the row; below `md` the grid stacks to one column and the horizontal gradient stops doing any sequencing work at all.

`ValueCard` renders an `<article>` whose title is a `<strong>`, not a heading. The cards therefore never appear in the document outline. `title` is `React.ReactNode`, so pass your own `<h3>` if these need to be navigable.
notFor: A row of equal-weight peers (a feature list, a set of capabilities). The whole point of the component is the tonal turn; used flat it is a worse plain card grid than `QuestionGrid` or `FeatureRow`.

Signalling a measured state. The `good | warn | danger` vocabulary bound to `semantic.matcha / warningAmber / errorRed` means an observed fact — that is `Finding` (or `ui/badge` on a product surface). `ValueCard`'s `cost` borrows `errorRed` for a marketing claim, and using it for real status teaches the reader that red means two different things.

decisions.title: A band with copy and a visual
decisions.verdict: Kept both. Prop names standardised — FeatureRow moved to lede/actions.
decisions.detail: Near-identical prop sets that disagreed on names for the same concepts: subtitle vs lede, action vs actions. The polarity difference is real — LightSectionCard carries the `light` class and inverts — so collapsing them behind a tone flag would hide a load-bearing accessibility mechanism behind something that looks like styling. Applied: FeatureRow renamed, all call sites updated.
evidence: FeatureRow: title, lede, children, actions, visual, reverse
LightSectionCard: title, lede, children, actions, visual, reverse

decisions.title: Small labels
decisions.verdict: Nine shapes, not the seven this decision carried for a fortnight. Chip extracted (PlanCard tier + WindowStatus). Badge/Eyebrow stay apart, now gated. StatChip/MetaChip keep the pill: a token gets the rectangle, prose gets the pill. TagChip vs CheckChip is the one still open — decided, not applied, because it moves pixels.
decisions.detail: PlanCard’s inline tier chip and WindowStatus were almost the same spec reached independently — rounded-[5px], font-mono, 10px, uppercase, px-[7px] py-1 — and disagreed on tracking alone, 0.05em against 0.08em. Earlier revisions of the table had no tracking column and recorded them as identical: an unmanaged cluster drifts in the column nobody is looking at. Applied 2026-08-12 as sections/chip.tsx, the tracking difference carried rather than flattened because both values shipped and were verified in a browser. The same failure then repeated one level up — the table caught a drift in a column it had, and could not catch a row it did not have, so TagChip and CheckChip were the same 11px mono tag written twice with the duplicate recorded only in evaluator-check.tsx’s own header. The table is a test now: __tests__/chip-cluster.test.ts pins every row against source and fails when a tenth shape lands unrecorded.

decisions.title: Texture behind content
decisions.verdict: No overlap once scoped. Pick by what you are dressing.
decisions.detail: SectionBackdrop is the field behind a mock inside a feature row. HeroBackdrop is a hero strip. DitheredMedia is a full hero composition. DitherOverlay is the raw layer for composing your own stack.

decisions.title: Framed content
decisions.verdict: No change. Different objects, read differently on purpose.
decisions.detail: Terminal is monospace with traffic lights and frames code or CLI output. ProductWindow frames a product mock and inverts to light by default, where light means the customer’s tool rather than Skene’s.

decisions.title: A track of steps
decisions.verdict: Kept both. The state vocabulary is the argument, not the geometry.
decisions.detail: Measured 2026-08-13 and near-identical: p-[22px] against p-7 (the same 22.4px), the same title and subtitle specs, the same flex-to-row list, the same 55% border / 12% fill ring mix, and connectors whose ml-[N] is the ring diameter halved in both. What differs is what a step MEANS — done | active | pending is progress, good | warn | danger is health — and a component that carried both would have to be told which vocabulary it is speaking. Same verdict as band-polarity: the difference is real and it is not styling.
evidence: PipelineStepper: 38px ring, ml-[18px] connector, done | active | pending
JourneyTrack: 34px ring, ml-[17px] connector, good | warn | danger

decisions.title: A card lifted out of its row
decisions.verdict: Kept both. The same card at inverted polarity.
decisions.detail: Identical radius, padding, lift and shadow token, and the same kicker → title → mt-auto list structure. The only difference is which way the theme points: PlanCard featured is cream in a dark grid, BridgeNode featured is near-black in a cream band. Collapsing them behind a tone prop is the exact move band-polarity rejected — it puts the light/dark class, which is load-bearing for legibility, behind a flag that reads as styling.
evidence: PlanCard featured: light border-brand-light bg-brand-light md:-translate-y-3, shadow-modal
BridgeNode featured: dark border-chrome-line-subtle bg-chrome-surface-1 md:-translate-y-3, shadow-modal

decisions.title: A terminal frame
decisions.verdict: One object drawn twice, at 8px and 12px. Neither is deprecated; the radii need settling.
decisions.detail: Same tokens, same 10px traffic lights, same mono body — but Terminal draws its frame from the .skene-terminal class in effects.css at 8px radius, and TerminalBlock draws its own through ArtPanel at 12px. Two terminals that do not match is worse than either. patterns/terminal is the documented one and has a case; TerminalBlock has the copy button, is the client boundary, and skene-site renders it on five routes. An @deprecated tag went on TerminalBlock briefly and was retracted the same day: it is the half with the feature, so the tag pointed readers away from the only one that could do the job. What actually needs settling is which radius wins, which is a visual decision and owed its own baseline movement.
evidence: effects.css .skene-terminal: --radius-panel (8px), traffic lights as a ::before
TerminalBlock: ArtPanel rounded-xl (12px), three explicit size-[10px] spans

decisions.title: The halftone field
decisions.verdict: Not equivalent, and not merged. Measured difference recorded.
decisions.detail: They load the SAME three image files under different key names — gh/db/jr against github/schema/journey — and independently arrived at the same 6% inset and 22rem floor. But ArtFrame also carries rounded-xl, an opaque bg-surface-deep-2 under the texture, and a non-row padding variant, so a merge changes pixels rather than being the neutral consolidation it looks like. Anyone taking it must predict the baseline diffs in the PR description before running the suite.

decisions.title: Tiles and cards that share a shell
decisions.verdict: Kept apart. Only the shell matches; the contents are different objects.
decisions.detail: OverviewTile and CheckResult have a byte-identical root class string, and ValueCard and QuestionCard share a 14px radius and 22.4px padding. Measured further, the insides disagree on purpose: OverviewTile is a 9px mono caption over a 24px number, CheckResult an 11px sans caption over 14px bold; the two cards carry different peach washes and different height floors. Extracting the shell would mean one shared line of classes and two components that still cannot be substituted, so it was not done. StatChip and MetaChip WERE collapsed onto a private Pill base, because there the whole box matched and only three tokens differed.

OverviewTile caption 9px mono 0.9px vs CheckResult 11px sans 0.16em
